mn71:6.2: It should be remembered that by tevijjā (Three True Knowledges) brahmins (and others) would understand the Three Vedas thoroughly learned by heart together with their ritual.
mn71:13.1: Ājīvaka ascetic: mentioned in Sutta 5, para. 31, on which Comy. remarks ‘a naked monk’ (MA. i, 151). It can be taken they were followers of Makkhali Gosāla and others, not orthodox brahmins, since they did not believe in kamma as the wanderers (paribbājaka) did. See Sutta 76, para. 61; also Sutta 60, para. 21, and the footnote to that para. on their leader.
mn71:14.3: Kammavāda—theory of action. Kiriyavāda—theory of doing: see Sutta 60, paras. 13-16.
